name: Social Environmental Features → Oxytocin Release → Prosocial Behavior

mechanism_chain.description: Face-to-face seating at conversational distance, shared activity surfaces, communal dining, co-located workstations → increased eye contact, sustained conversation, physical proximity, shared rhythmic activity. Tier 1 calibration.

data.finding: Face-to-face seating at conversational distance produces more eye contact, conversation, and longer social interactions than parallel seating
data.paradigm: Observational studies of seating arrangement effects
data.effect: d ≈ 0.50-0.70 for seating arrangement on social interaction

justification.backing: The architectural → social behavior link is well-supported independent of the OT mechanism. Spaces that facilitate face-to-face orientation at conversational distance (1.2-3.5 m) produce the social behaviors that may trigger OT release.
justification.qualifier: This step is the confidence bottleneck. The architectural-to-behavior link is solid (d ≈ 0.50-0.70); the behavior-to-OT link in Step 2 is where confidence attenuates.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if architectural features have minimal effect on social interaction patterns; but observational evidence strongly supports the link.

mechanism_chain.description: Sustained eye contact > 30s, physical touch (C-tactile optimal velocity), synchronous activity → central OT release from PVN magnocellular neurons (dendritic release) and posterior pituitary (peripheral release). Young & Wang 2004; Uvnäs-Moberg et al. 2015.

data.finding: Sustained mutual gaze > 30s triggers measurable peripheral OT increase
data.paradigm: Human-dog gaze studies with OT measurement

data.finding: Physical touch at C-tactile optimal velocity (1-10 cm/s) triggers OT release

justification.backing: Young's molecular mechanism is well-characterized: OT is released from PVN magnocellular neurons (central) and posterior pituitary (peripheral) in response to specific social stimuli. The conditions that trigger release are established.
justification.qualifier: Molecular mechanism confidence is high (0.85 in animal models); human application is somewhat lower (0.65) due to reliance on peripheral OT measurement.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if peripheral OT measurement does not reflect central OT release; or if human OT dynamics differ substantially from animal models.

mechanism_chain.description: OT acts on OXTR in nucleus accumbens, ventral pallidum, mPFC → increased trust, social approach, facial expression recognition, cooperative behavior. Kosfeld et al. 2005; Domes et al. 2007.

data.finding: Intranasal OT administration increases trust in economic games
data.paradigm: Trust game with OT vs. placebo

data.finding: Intranasal OT enhances facial expression recognition
data.paradigm: Emotion recognition task with OT vs. placebo

justification.backing: The OT → prosocial behavior link is well-established through intranasal OT administration studies. The receptor distribution (OXTR in nucleus accumbens, ventral pallidum, mPFC) is the mechanistic substrate from Young's molecular work.
justification.qualifier: Intranasal OT produces supraphysiological brain concentrations; effects from endogenous OT release may be smaller. The ANALOGICAL bridge warrant (0.35) applies to the architectural deployment.
justification.rebuttal: Would fail if endogenous OT levels from architectural-facilitated social behaviors are insufficient to produce measurable behavioral effects.

eye_contact_threshold.note: Sustained mutual gaze > 30s triggers measurable peripheral OT increase. Nagasawa et al. 2015.

physical_touch_condition.note: C-tactile affective touch — see MULTI-I panel CT_AFFECTIVE_TOUCH_001

social_setting_features.note: These are molecular/behavioral parameters from Young's calibration. The architectural bridge (Step 1 → Step 2) is the confidence bottleneck.

bridge_warrant_score.note: Full architectural → OT → prosocial chain has low composite credence. Builder AI should use Tier 1 parameters (architectural → social behavior) directly.

ie_dpt_interaction: No direct IE-DPT interaction identified for this template.
key_references: Young, L. J., & Wang, Z. (2004). https://doi.org/10.1038/nn1327

cross_template_interactions.IC2: Body Budget Prediction — OT has an anxiolytic, stress-buffering effect (reduces cortisol reactivity). When OT release conditions are met, IC2 body-budget prediction shifts toward reduced allostatic cost. This is a positive IC2 interaction — the template reduces body-budget expenditure.
cross_template_interactions.AX4: Perceived Control — voluntary participation in shared social activity (vs. forced communal activity in institutional settings) is critical. Involuntary communal dining in a locked ward does not produce the same OT benefit as voluntary shared meals.
